summary: Evidence package request: Siemplify playbook sample + crosswalk to Redwood audit fields
description:
Issue summary: Customer (SentinelCore) is preparing a SOC playbook automation using Siemplify and has requested a sample delivery of Redwood audit events plus a field crosswalk that maps Redwood audit schema to Siemplify playbook variables.

Impact: Security operations team cannot finalize incident enrichment playbooks until they have a) a representative sample of normalized audit events, b) a mapping that shows which Redwood audit fields correspond to Siemplify variables, and c) proof that tenant-scoped PII is pseudonymized according to customer policy. The delay is blocking the next-phase SOC validation.

Request details: Customer requested the following deliverables: 1) a zipped sample (max 500 events) of real-format audit events in JSON Lines (ndjson) with timestamps in UTC and canonicalized field names; 2) a CSV crosswalk mapping Redwood field names to recommended Siemplify variable names and example transformation rules (e.g., hash algorithm, salt handling); 3) a short verification note describing redaction/pseudonymization applied and KMS key rotation metadata; 4) an example Siemplify inbound connector configuration (HTTP webhook + HMAC) that demonstrates signature verification and replay window; 5) guidance on ingest time canonicalization (milliseconds vs seconds) and timezone handling.

Acceptable formats: ndjson for events, CSV for crosswalk, PEM or JWK excerpt for verification, and a tiny sample webhook config block.

Deadline: Customer requests delivery by 2026-03-14 to align with their internal compliance run.

Contact: Primary SE: Aisha Patel (reporter). Customer contact: Daniel Ng (SentinelCore SOC lead).

Notes: This is an evidence-style request (not a product change). Sensitive data must be pseudonymized; do not include full unredacted user identifiers in the sample. If customer insists on raw events, escalate to Security with a signed NDA/occasional gating.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer reviewed Redwood audit export docs and attempted to map fields to Siemplify variables; requested a canonical example to avoid mis-mapping.
2) Customer tried a small test by piping a live webhook to their dev Siemplify instance; signature mismatch occurred (reported separately).
3) Customer is unable to complete playbook unit tests without a sample crosswalk, and flagged a blocker to SOC leadership.
logs: Connector attempt logs: customer reports 401 on inbound test webhook at 2026-03-09T15:20:00Z; support inspected api-gateway and saw HMAC verification failures in 5/5 sample attempts (trace id: api-trace-78a1).
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after call with Daniel Ng. Action: prepare sample ndjson + crosswalk and propose pseudonymization approach.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Noted HMAC mismatch; asked customer to confirm header names and shared example of expected signature calculation. Linked PR with example verification code: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-exporter/pull/412
2026-03-11 - Daniel Ng (Customer): Will accept pseudonymized sample; requests that we use HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-specific salt and include replay-window guidance.

2026-03-12 - Miguel Torres (SRE): Prepared preliminary crosswalk CSV and pseudonymization note; uploaded to internal draft bucket and asking Security for approval to share artifacts. Security slack thread: #security-evidence (see slack thread link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C08... ).
investigation_notes: Confirmed audit-exporter can emit ndjson with timestamp precision to milliseconds and with tenant-scoped envelope when requested.
Existing webhook examples in repo use X-Redwood-Signature and X-Redwood-Timestamp headers; customer was using X-SIEM-Signature by mistake (caused 401s).

Draft crosswalk includes transformations: actor => siemplify.actor_id (sha256 with tenant salt), actor_email => siemplify.actor_email_pseud (partial redaction + tokenization), event_context.user_agent => siemplify.user_agent, model => siemplify.model_name.
Security requested KMS key artifact and rotation window; SRE prepared proof of last rotation date (2026-02-28) and CMK alias; awaiting Security sign-off to include in outbound artifact bundle.
Potential follow-up: add native Siemplify connector template to audit-exporter repo if customer wants long-term managed connector.
resolution: Pending: Draft artifacts prepared (ndjson sample and crosswalk CSV). Awaiting Security approval for pseudonymization verification snippets and explicit sign-off from customer on the pseudonymization method. Next step after approval: deliver zipped evidence bundle via secure transfer and provide a short walk-through call with the SOC team.
